title: Crashing a project
log: 2026-11-01T14:46:39Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point only teaches what the critical path is and how delays on it affect the project, but not crashing, which is shortening activities at a cost and checking whether the critical path moves, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Crashing a project
card: Crashing means shortening an activity by spending extra money. Each activity has a crash cost for every time unit saved.
The project time falls only if you crash an activity on the critical path, the longest path through the network.
To cut the time at least cost, crash the cheapest critical activity first. Once a path is shortened to match another path, both paths are critical.
Example: path 1 takes 9 days and path 2 takes 8. Crashing a path 1 activity by 1 day gives 8 days. Now both paths are critical, so any further cut needs both paths shortened.
draft.remember: Crash only critical activities, cheapest first, and check if the critical path changes.

a.q: The critical path is A, C, E (14 days). Path B, D takes 10 days. Crash costs per day: A $300, C $500, D $100, E $400. Which activity should be crashed to cut 1 day at least cost?
a.why: Only activities on the critical path can shorten the project. Of A, C and E, activity A is cheapest. D costs less but is not critical, so crashing it does not shorten the project.
a.clue: Cross out any activity that is not on the critical path.

b.q: Path X takes 12 days and path Y takes 11 days. An activity only on X can be crashed by up to 3 days, at $200 a day. If all 3 days are crashed, how many days does the project time fall by?
b.why: After 1 day, X takes 11 days and matches Y. Y is now critical and still takes 11 days, so the project time stays at 11. The other 2 days of crashing cost money but save no time.
b.clue: Which path sets the time once X becomes shorter than Y?
